convoLines.text: "I asked Theo about the most useful thing you've learned — Theo's gone. What's the most useful thing you've learned since we got here?"
"The fundamental skill. Everything else is decoration."
The warmth pulls back a notch. They're weighing something.
"...What's that supposed to mean?" Their voice goes careful.
"Still on the most useful thing you've learned."
"Not right now. I've got my own things to handle."
"Sorry — I shouldn't load that on you. What's up?"
They go very still. Not relaxed-still. Held-still.

A wall comes down, then — surprisingly — a door opens behind it. "I don't actually want to belong somewhere. I want to find their family. I wasn't protecting myself. I was protecting someone else." Quiet. Real.
They fill the quiet. "Anyway — where was I?"
"...I need to go be quiet for a while."
"Good talk. I feel like I know you a little better now."
"What do you make of all this? Really."
"Bleak. Probably true. I keep looking for the part where it's not."
"There's more, but that's for another fire."
"I think we're an experiment someone forgot to label. And the unlabeled part is what scares me — it means nobody's coming to check the results."
"Still on what you make of all this."
"...Fine. This had better be worth it."
"Forget I said anything. What did you want?"
"You want to know about that? Okay." "Theo owed me a favor. I keep thinking about collecting. Stupid."
"A name. Okay." You say it out loud, trying the shape of it:
"Roles. Not ranks — promises."
"I pace while thinking. It doesn't bring anyone back. It just keeps my hands from shaking."
"Oh — okay. Later, then."
"Good talk. I feel like I know you a little better now."
"This was good." They mean it.
"About that question — What's the worst thing you've done since the sky changed?"
No judgment in their face. "We're all doing math that doesn't add up. You're still here. That counts."
Their friendliness thins — still there, just held at arm's length.
"Still on the worst thing you've done."
"Not right now. I've got my own things to handle."
"Forget I said anything. What did you want?"
"Theo always took the burnt piece. Said someone had to. I take it now."
"I should go. You know where to find me."
A comfortable quiet settles. They smile a little, and let it be.
"Good talk. I feel like I know you a little better now."
"This was good." They mean it.
"About that question — Teach me something. Anything you know that I don't."
"All right. Show me when we work together. I need you to hear that."
The ease drains out of it, a little.
"Can I be honest? Still on teaching them something."
"Sorry — I shouldn't load that on you. What's up?"
"Good question." "Last time things were different. They always are." "Since Theo died... I keep expecting to see Theo at the fire. Stupid."
"I'm picking up Theo's share of the work. Someone should, and it might as well be me."
"Roles. Not ranks — promises."
"Well." A breath. "That's where things stand."
You show them Wild Onion — where it grows, how to tell it apart. A short laugh. "And I've been walking past it for weeks."
"Right. Go on, then."
"Good talk. I feel like I know you a little better now."
They're smiling as you go. "Come back anytime."
"Do you still sing? ...Sorry — weird question. I just realized I haven't heard anyone sing."
"Ha! The creek concerts. I've heard those. Keep going."
"Under my breath, when I'm working. Old songs from Columbus, Ohio. The words are half gone but the tune holds. Tunes outlast everything."
"Practical view: Still on whether you still sing."
"Not right now. I've got my own things to handle."
"Sorry — I shouldn't load that on you. What's up? Worth considering."
"You asked me that before. It's a different question now." "Have you seen the sick row? 2 down with a hot angry fever. Nobody says it out loud but everyone's counting."
"Okay. We'll pick this up later."
You say nothing. Neither do they, for a while — and it's fine.
"Good talk. I feel like I know you a little better now."
They're smiling as you go. "Come back anytime."
"About your read on people here — Got a read on anyone here yet? Who should I be watching?"
"Same. But keep your eyes open — some people here are performing, not surviving."
"a cellar full of jars — I'll show you on the map sometime. It's real."
"a ridge with a view for miles — I'll show you on the map sometime. It's real."
The ease drains out of it, a little.
"Still on your read on people here."
"I work alone. Nothing personal. ...It's a little personal."
"Forget I said anything. What did you want?"
"2 of us are down with a hot angry fever. Boil everything. I mean everything."
You show them Ghost Pipe — where it grows, how to tell it apart. "Huh." They turn it over in their mind. "I'll remember that one."
"I don't sleep much when the sick row's full. I do push-ups at dawn instead."
"I should go. You know where to find me."
A comfortable quiet settles. They smile a little, and let it be.
"Good talk. I feel like I know you a little better now."
They're smiling as you go. "Come back anytime."

"This one — Tamarind. Leaf, stem, smell. You won't forget it now."
They answer at length. They nod back, slowly. "Food?"
They answer at length. A grin breaks through, quick and warm.
They answer at length. You tap your chest, then theirs. Us. They nod, emphatic.
You listen hard, watching their mouth shape the words. Sounds, and the shape of meaning just out of reach.
They speak; the translation falters.
They glance toward their own thoughts; the exchange is winding down.
A comfortable quiet settles. They smile a little, and let it be.
"This was good." They mean it.
"I can't reach this properly. Could you take a look?"
"It's getting worse, not better. If it festers I'm no good to anyone — can't haul, can't hunt, can't watch. Just clean it out and wrap it tight."
Move next to them, on the same side of the Haven door, to help.
"Sorry — I shouldn't load that on you. What's up?"
"We lost Enrique and Paisley this week. I keep setting out extra portions. Stupid."
"Okay. Yeah. I trust you."
"Walk my trap line with me? Extra hands, extra eyes."
Ines has been stockpiling where nobody looks. "Take half. You've got the hands for it." (+4 wood, +4 fiber to the village stash.)
"I memorize the stars. It doesn't bring anyone back. It just keeps my hands from shaking."
"Roles. Not ranks — promises."
"We bury, we grieve, we keep going. There's no step four."
"Still on what's been happening."
"Oh — okay. Later, then."
"...Think about it? I'll be around."
They're smiling as you go. "Come back anytime."
